text:
Predicates:
SpottedNearCampus(x) ::: x can be spotted near the campus.
Cute(x) ::: x is cute.
Turtle(x) ::: x is a turtle.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Skittish(x) ::: x is skittish.
Calm(x) ::: x is calm.
Squirrel(x) ::: x is a squirrel.
Rockie ::: Rockie (a particular animal)
Premises:
∀x (SpottedNearCampus(x) ∧ Rabbit(x)) → Cute(x) ::: All rabbits that can be spotted near the campus are cute.
∃x (Turtle(x) ∧ SpottedNearCampus(x)) ::: Some turtles can be spotted near the campus.
∀x (Squirrel(x) ∧ SpottedNearCampus(x)) → Skittish(x) ::: All squirrels that can be spotted near the campus are skittish.
SpottedNearCampus(Rockie) ::: Rockie can be spotted near the campus.
¬(Calm(Rockie)) ::: Rockie is not calm.
Premises:
Rockie can be spotted near the campus and is calm, which contrasts with the previous statement that Rockie is not calm.
Conclusion:
(¬(Turtle(Rockie) ∧ Squirrel(Rockie))) → (Cute(Rockie) ∨ Skittish(Rockie)) ::: If Rockie is not both a turtle and a squirrel, then Rockie is either cute or skittish.
